intent: WP-0G (TIT-008): strict DocOps convergence. commit.message: feat(docops): WP-0G strict convergence and checked reconcile delivery (TIT-008)

interface_mismatches: INTERFACE_MISMATCH_MAP.md carries no open entry for the DocOps script/workflow surfaces at base 1e806bd.
honest_blockers: The spec lists tests/test_docops_reconcile_workflow.py and tests/test_pr_dedupe_workflow.py as new; test_pr_dedupe_workflow.py already exists on main (landed via PR #985) with jq-driven behavioral coverage of exactly the spec's timestamped-snapshot-without-marker cases, so this packet adds only the reconcile-delivery contract file and leaves the existing dedupe tests untouched.

Strict DocOps green is bound to THIS exact tree: every sibling Wave-1 PR that adds test files re-stales the counts on merge, and the repaired reconcile workflow is the mechanism that re-converges main afterward; merging this PR last (or letting the reconcile lane run) is the expected sequence.

The reconcile workflow's Tier-2 checks-verification can only prove delivery health in CI; on a token-less host it is structural-test evidence only. The operator prerequisite (DOCOPS_RECONCILE_TOKEN or explicit reviewed-PR fallback) from the spec remains open and is what the new red path names.
scripts/docops/check_docops_integrity.py itself needed no change: strict mode, the writers, and the report JSON already behave per spec; the drift was pure count staleness plus the delivery gap.
Packet pytest gates run under the runner-admitted system python3 with repo deps importable via the system dist-packages editable install performed this session.
make test-fast on this host fails only on the known tests/conformance/test_repo_ratchet_holds.py 10s-timeout flake; per-occurrence re-proof is recorded in the PR body.
session_entry.rollback: Revert the regenerated count surfaces, the reconcile workflow, and the tests together; never hand-edit generated counts (spec WP-0G rollback rule).
